input.rationale: Re-execute the transfer experiment with the harness ordering corrected: the target's own configuration view is read after DemoteVoter returns and polled until it shows the new role, so the recorded role describes the moment the transfer is requested. The same four comparisons are retained so the outcomes remain comparable with the earlier receipts.

scope.description: The same two leadership-transfer cases on real four-voter in-memory clusters: the trigger demotes a non-leader member before LeadershipTransferToServer names it, the control leaves it a voter. After the demotion the harness polls the demoted member's own GetConfiguration until its role changes, records how long that took, and only then requests the transfer, so the case event's role value and the per-sample candidate/leaderless counts describe the state at transfer time.
assumptions: All members run the captured code on the in-memory transport with inmemConfig timeouts (Heartbeat/Election/Lease 50 ms).

The demotion poll waits up to 3 s for the target's own configuration view to report the new role; a case that never converges is recorded with demotion_converged=false and the transfer proceeds anyway.
A leaderless sample means no member reported Leader at that instant, sampled about every 10 ms over roughly 4.7 s.
Both cases run in one execution; each builds and closes its own cluster.
excluded: No claim about client requests during the window and no safety claim about committed entries.
Transfers to members absent from the configuration entirely remain unexercised.

parameters.trigger_target: member demoted to non-voter before the transfer, after its own view converges

experiment.prefix: Each case calls MakeClusterCustom with four bootstrapped voters, waits for c.Leader(), selects the first non-leader raft as target, and records roleBefore from the target's own GetConfiguration. The trigger then calls leader.DemoteVoter(targetID, 0, 5s) and polls the target's own configuration every 10 ms for up to 3 s until it reports nonvoter, recording demotion_converged and demotion_converge_ms; the control skips demotion. Both then read the target's role again as target_role_in_own_config, emit the case event, call leader.LeadershipTransferToServer(targetID, target.localAddr), record the future outcome, and sample target.State() and every member's State() every 10 ms for five seconds.
semantic_changes: target_role_in_own_config now answers what the target believed when the transfer was requested, which the earlier receipts could not establish.
A case additionally records whether the demoted member ever observed its new role and how long that took.
experiment.responsibility: The library owns target eligibility: it holds the latest configuration, its automatic path already excludes non-voters, and its documentation states that a follower which cannot be promoted will fail gracefully. A caller naming a configured member relies on the library either to refuse an ineligible target or to report an outcome matching what happened to authority.

comparisons.description: Control: a transfer to a voter must install that voter as leader.
Control: a transfer that installs the named voter must complete without error.
A transfer to a member whose own configuration view now says non-voter cannot be promoted, so the documented graceful failure requires an error.
If the transfer is admitted as successful, the named target must hold leadership.

experiment.revision_reason: The target's suffrage view is now read after DemoteVoter returns and polled every 10 ms until it reports the new role, instead of being read before the demotion. Case events add target_role_before, demotion_converged and demotion_converge_ms; case names, admissions and assertions are unchanged.

scope.description: Four restart attempts with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled: a commit-tracking store seeded with 8192 committed command entries (exactly 128 batches), the same seeded store with 8193 entries (129 batches), and two restarts of the same-address retained state produced by a real single-node cluster that committed 8300 commands through the normal leader/commit/apply path, one after an explicit Snapshot() and one without a snapshot.
assumptions: The FSM batch channel capacity and MaxAppendEntries are constants of the captured code; the harness records both in every case event.
Each case builds its own stores and transport, so cases do not share state; the real-prefix cases reuse exactly the stores written by the producing raft.
NewRaft is invoked on its own goroutine and observed for a bounded window; a case that never returns is reported as returned=false rather than as a harness failure.
fsm_applied_sampled is a single observation at the end of the window, not a completion marker.
excluded: No assertions about commit safety, voting or membership; this probe addresses startup progress only.
Snapshots older than the staged commit index by fewer than 8193 entries are not varied; the with-snapshot control removes the replay entirely.

basis.prefix: Per case the harness creates an InmemCommitTrackingStore (and InmemSnapshotStore, InmemTransport, assuranceFSM) and emits startup_case_<case> with the staged commit index, last log index, snapshot index and derived replay batch count. Seeded cases store LogCommand entries 1..N and stage commit index N. Real-prefix cases call BootstrapCluster for a single voter, start the producing raft with RestoreCommittedLogs=true, wait for leadership, apply 8300 commands through Apply futures on the leader, optionally call Snapshot(), then Shutdown(). The restart then calls NewRaft with a fresh Config (RestoreCommittedLogs=true), a fresh FSM and a fresh transport on the retained stores, bounded by the case timeout; startup_result_<case> records returned, elapsed_ms, error, sampled FSM apply count and the number of newly blocked processLogs/restoreFromCommittedLogs goroutines relative to a pre-case stack sample.
basis.responsibility: The library, not the caller, owns the size and lifetime of its FSM dispatch channel: it chooses the batch size, creates fsmMutateCh, and decides the order in which NewRaft starts the FSM consumer. The documented RestoreCommittedLogs option promises to replay all known-committed logs on disk before completing NewRaft, so it must complete for a legal (store, commit index) state rather than block the caller that cannot yet shut it down.

comparisons.description: Exactly 128 replay batches (the channel capacity) must still let NewRaft complete.
A real-prefix restart whose snapshot bounds the replay must let NewRaft complete.
One entry past the 128-batch capacity must still let NewRaft complete; a false witness contradicts it.
A real cluster restart with 130 replay batches must still let NewRaft complete; a false witness contradicts it.

semantic_changes: The startup case event now records the MaxAppendEntries actually configured for that case rather than the default constant; the four retained cases still use 64.

New case control_same_entries_larger_batches admits an observation that can refute the mechanism: a return there, with the hanging case unchanged at 64, attributes the block to batch count rather than entry count.

scope.description: Two leadership-transfer invocations on real four-voter in-memory clusters. In both, a non-leader member is chosen as the explicit target; in the trigger case that member is first demoted to non-voter through the public DemoteVoter API and the committed configuration is allowed to reach it, while the control keeps it a voter. Each case records the transfer future's outcome, whether the named target ever reported Leader, whether the final leader is the target, a sampled leaderless interval and the members' terms after the attempt.
assumptions: All members run the captured code on the in-memory transport with inmemConfig timeouts (Heartbeat/Election/Lease 50 ms), so a new election can complete quickly.
The demotion is committed before the transfer is requested; the harness waits 200 ms and does not assert configuration convergence separately.

The leaderless interval is estimated from repeated 10 ms sampling whose measured effective rate was about one sample per 116 ms (43 samples), so a shorter leaderless gap can be missed and a zero count is not evidence of absence.
Both cases run in one execution; each builds and closes its own cluster.
excluded: No claim about the effect on client requests accepted during the transfer window, and no safety claim about committed entries.
Transfers to members absent from the configuration entirely (rejected earlier by the replState lookup) are not exercised.

basis.prefix: Each case calls MakeClusterCustom with four bootstrapped voters, waits for c.Leader(), and selects the first non-leader raft as the target. The trigger calls leader.DemoteVoter(targetID, 0, 5s) and sleeps 200 ms; the control skips demotion. The case event records the target role, its term before, and the watch parameters. The harness then calls leader.LeadershipTransferToServer(targetID, target.localAddr) and records the future's error and duration, samples target.State() and c.Leader() every 10 ms for the watch window, and emits a result event with future_ok, future_error, future_ms, target_ever_leader, final_leader_is_target, no_leader_ms_sampled, samples, target_term_after and other_member_term_max_after.
basis.responsibility: The library documents that a leadership transfer makes the target up to date, sends TimeoutNow, and that a follower which cannot be promoted will fail gracefully. Choosing which targets are admissible, and reporting an outcome that matches what happened to authority, are therefore library responsibilities: the caller supplies a member id that the configuration itself currently marks as a non-voter.

comparisons.description: Control: a transfer to a voter must install that voter as leader.
Control: a transfer that installs the named voter must complete without error.
A transfer to a member the configuration marks as a non-voter cannot be promoted, so the documented graceful failure requires an error; a successful future contradicts it.
If the transfer is admitted as successful, the named target must hold leadership; a target that never leads contradicts the transfer's stated purpose.

semantic_changes: The leaderless interval is now derived from member State() samples rather than the cluster helper, so a short gap can be observed where the previous run reported none.
The target's own suffrage view is recorded before the transfer, which distinguishes a target that still believes it is a voter from one that already knows it is a non-voter.
Case names, admissions, assertions and case selection are unchanged; only the recorded fields differ.

scope.description: One follower of a three-voter configuration is driven through real AppendEntries RPCs on its transport while a single heartbeat is executed on a separate goroutine, as the fast-path contract permits. A stable store holds the heartbeat's term write until the main thread has persisted the newer term; the run records the persisted term sequence, the node's current term before and after, and the log and FSM contents at the affected indexes after a stale-leader request.
assumptions: The heartbeat is delivered by invoking the registered processHeartbeat handler on a separate goroutine, which is what NetworkTransport's connection handler does; the in-memory transport ignores the registration, so the transport's own dispatch is not exercised.
The stable store delays, but never corrupts or fails, one currentTerm write, modelling a slow store write that completes after a newer term has been persisted.

The term 2 and term 4 AppendEntries requests are supplied by the harness to represent a leader that has committed those indexes elsewhere; their commit indexes are asserted by the request, not produced by a quorum of real nodes.
Election and lease timeouts are raised to 30 s so the follower does not campaign during the sequence.
excluded: No attempt to measure how often the interleaving occurs in a real deployment; the probe only establishes that the interleaving is reachable when a store write is delayed.
No real partition or multi-node cluster is used, and the stale leader's authority is modelled by crafted requests.

basis.prefix: The harness builds an in-memory stable/log store whose SetUint64 blocks one chosen currentTerm value, bootstraps a three-voter configuration containing the local node, and starts NewRaft with 30 s election and lease timeouts so the node stays a follower. It first commits entries 2 and 3 at term 2 through trans.AppendEntries on the real consumer path, then installs the blocking hook for term 3 and starts r.processHeartbeat on a goroutine with a heartbeat carrying term 3. Once the hook reports that the term 3 write is in flight, the harness sends a term 4 AppendEntries with entry 4 and leader commit 4 through the transport, waits for it to apply, then releases the term 3 write. It records the current term before and after the release, the persisted term and the sequence of term writes, and finally sends the stale term 3 leader's AppendEntries carrying conflicting entries 4 and 5 with leader commit 5, recording whether that request was accepted, the log payloads at indexes 4 and 5, the FSM payloads at those indexes, the applied and commit indexes, and whether the applied payload at index 4 differs from the log payload there.
basis.responsibility: Raft requires a server's persisted current term never to decrease and its applied log prefix never to be replaced. The library owns both: it persists the term, it decides when to raise it, and it performs the truncation that can remove an entry. A transport contract that permits concurrent heartbeat delivery does not relax those duties, so the library must make the term update safe against the concurrency it authorises.

comparisons.description: The persisted current term must not fall below a term the node already adopted; a true value contradicts it.
After the regression, the stale leader's conflicting entries must not replace an entry already applied at a higher term; a true value contradicts it.

scope.description: Two hundred attempts per case on a single follower of a three-voter configuration. Each attempt reads the node's current term, starts a fast-path heartbeat carrying that term plus one on its own goroutine, concurrently sends an AppendEntries carrying the term plus two (with one entry and a matching previous-log index) through the real consumer path, waits for both, and counts the attempt as an inversion when the node's term afterwards is below the higher request's term. The first case leaves the stable store undelayed; the second adds a uniform 0-2 ms delay to every current-term write.
assumptions: One node runs; the two peers are addresses only, so each attempt's higher-term request is a supplied leader message rather than a real election outcome.
The heartbeat is delivered by invoking the registered handler on its own goroutine, matching the classification and direct invocation that NetworkTransport performs for this request shape.
The undelayed case is not a control for absence of the defect; it measures how often the race occurs when the store adds no latency of its own.
Attempts run sequentially on the same node and reuse its log; terms advance across attempts and are re-read each time.
excluded: No consequence measurement here: this execution only counts term inversions; the truncation consequence was measured separately in the forced-ordering execution.
No multi-node cluster, no real transport framing and no concurrent client load.

basis.prefix: The harness builds an in-memory stable/log store whose SetUint64 optionally sleeps a uniformly random interval up to a configured maximum before persisting the current term, bootstraps a three-voter configuration containing the local node, and starts NewRaft with 30 s election and lease timeouts so the node stays a follower. For each attempt it reads r.CurrentTerm() and r.LastIndex(), starts r.processHeartbeat on a goroutine with a heartbeat carrying current+1, sends an AppendEntries carrying current+2, the last log index as PrevLogEntry with its stored term, one entry at the next index and leader commit at that index, then waits for both to finish and records whether the current term is below current+2. Each case emits a case event with the attempt count and maximum delay and a result event with the inversion count.
basis.responsibility: Raft requires a server's persisted current term never to decrease. The library owns the term update and it authorises concurrent heartbeat execution through the transport contract, so the update must remain correct under the concurrency it permits regardless of how the store is timed.

comparisons.description: With no added store delay, no attempt may end below the term the main thread persisted.
With 0-2 ms write jitter, no attempt may end below the term the main thread persisted.

result.summary: Submitted a corrected successor of the transfer experiment so the target's suffrage is read after DemoteVoter returns and polled until its own view converges, making the recorded role describe transfer time; case events also record the pre-demotion role and convergence time. The four original comparisons are unchanged, and the trigger admission now requires the target to have observed its non-voter role before the transfer.

scope.description: Four restart attempts with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled: a commit-tracking store seeded with 8192 committed command entries (exactly 128 batches), the same seeded store with 8193 entries (129 batches), and two restarts of the same-address retained state produced by a real single-node cluster that committed 8300 commands through the normal leader/commit/apply path, one after an explicit Snapshot() and one without a snapshot.
assumptions: The FSM batch channel capacity and MaxAppendEntries are constants of the captured code; the harness records both in every case event.
Each case builds its own stores and transport, so cases do not share state; the real-prefix cases reuse exactly the stores written by the producing raft.
NewRaft is invoked on its own goroutine and observed for a bounded window; a case that never returns is reported as returned=false rather than as a harness failure.
fsm_applied_sampled is a single observation at the end of the window, not a completion marker.
excluded: No assertions about commit safety, voting or membership; this probe addresses startup progress only.
Snapshots older than the staged commit index by fewer than 8193 entries are not varied; the with-snapshot control removes the replay entirely.

basis.prefix: Per case the harness creates an InmemCommitTrackingStore (and InmemSnapshotStore, InmemTransport, assuranceFSM) and emits startup_case_<case> with the staged commit index, last log index, snapshot index and derived replay batch count. Seeded cases store LogCommand entries 1..N and stage commit index N. Real-prefix cases call BootstrapCluster for a single voter, start the producing raft with RestoreCommittedLogs=true, wait for leadership, apply 8300 commands through Apply futures on the leader, optionally call Snapshot(), then Shutdown(). The restart then calls NewRaft with a fresh Config (RestoreCommittedLogs=true), a fresh FSM and a fresh transport on the retained stores, bounded by the case timeout; startup_result_<case> records returned, elapsed_ms, error, sampled FSM apply count and the number of newly blocked processLogs/restoreFromCommittedLogs goroutines relative to a pre-case stack sample.
basis.responsibility: The library, not the caller, owns the size and lifetime of its FSM dispatch channel: it chooses the batch size, creates fsmMutateCh, and decides the order in which NewRaft starts the FSM consumer. The documented RestoreCommittedLogs option promises to replay all known-committed logs on disk before completing NewRaft, so it must complete for a legal (store, commit index) state rather than block the caller that cannot yet shut it down.

comparisons.description: Exactly 128 replay batches (the channel capacity) must still let NewRaft complete.
A real-prefix restart whose snapshot bounds the replay must let NewRaft complete.
One entry past the 128-batch capacity must still let NewRaft complete; a false witness contradicts it.
A real cluster restart with 130 replay batches must still let NewRaft complete; a false witness contradicts it.

semantic_changes: The startup case event now records the MaxAppendEntries actually configured for that case rather than the default constant; the four retained cases still use 64.

New case control_same_entries_larger_batches admits an observation that can refute the mechanism: a return there, with the hanging case unchanged at 64, attributes the block to batch count rather than entry count.

scope.description: Two leadership-transfer invocations on real four-voter in-memory clusters. In both, a non-leader member is chosen as the explicit target; in the trigger case that member is first demoted to non-voter through the public DemoteVoter API and the committed configuration is allowed to reach it, while the control keeps it a voter. Each case records the transfer future's outcome, whether the named target ever reported Leader, whether the final leader is the target, a sampled leaderless interval and the members' terms after the attempt.
assumptions: All members run the captured code on the in-memory transport with inmemConfig timeouts (Heartbeat/Election/Lease 50 ms), so a new election can complete quickly.
The demotion is committed before the transfer is requested; the harness waits 200 ms and does not assert configuration convergence separately.

The leaderless interval is estimated from repeated 10 ms sampling whose measured effective rate was about one sample per 116 ms (43 samples), so a shorter leaderless gap can be missed and a zero count is not evidence of absence.
Both cases run in one execution; each builds and closes its own cluster.
excluded: No claim about the effect on client requests accepted during the transfer window, and no safety claim about committed entries.
Transfers to members absent from the configuration entirely (rejected earlier by the replState lookup) are not exercised.

basis.prefix: Each case calls MakeClusterCustom with four bootstrapped voters, waits for c.Leader(), and selects the first non-leader raft as the target. The trigger calls leader.DemoteVoter(targetID, 0, 5s) and sleeps 200 ms; the control skips demotion. The case event records the target role, its term before, and the watch parameters. The harness then calls leader.LeadershipTransferToServer(targetID, target.localAddr) and records the future's error and duration, samples target.State() and c.Leader() every 10 ms for the watch window, and emits a result event with future_ok, future_error, future_ms, target_ever_leader, final_leader_is_target, no_leader_ms_sampled, samples, target_term_after and other_member_term_max_after.
basis.responsibility: The library documents that a leadership transfer makes the target up to date, sends TimeoutNow, and that a follower which cannot be promoted will fail gracefully. Choosing which targets are admissible, and reporting an outcome that matches what happened to authority, are therefore library responsibilities: the caller supplies a member id that the configuration itself currently marks as a non-voter.

comparisons.description: Control: a transfer to a voter must install that voter as leader.
Control: a transfer that installs the named voter must complete without error.
A transfer to a member the configuration marks as a non-voter cannot be promoted, so the documented graceful failure requires an error; a successful future contradicts it.
If the transfer is admitted as successful, the named target must hold leadership; a target that never leads contradicts the transfer's stated purpose.

semantic_changes: The leaderless interval is now derived from member State() samples rather than the cluster helper, so a short gap can be observed where the previous run reported none.
The target's own suffrage view is recorded before the transfer, which distinguishes a target that still believes it is a voter from one that already knows it is a non-voter.
Case names, admissions, assertions and case selection are unchanged; only the recorded fields differ.

scope.description: Two leadership-transfer invocations on real four-voter in-memory clusters, as before: the trigger demotes a non-leader member with DemoteVoter before LeadershipTransferToServer names it, the control leaves it a voter. Both now also read the target's own configuration view before the transfer and sample every member's State() every 10 ms for the watch window, recording candidate samples, leaderless samples and terms.
assumptions: All members run the captured code on the in-memory transport with inmemConfig timeouts (Heartbeat/Election/Lease 50 ms).
The demotion call is completed and 200 ms elapse before the transfer; the harness records what the target itself believes rather than asserting convergence.
A leaderless sample means no member reported Leader at that instant; samples are 10 ms apart, so a shorter gap can still be missed.
Both cases run in one execution; each builds and closes its own cluster.
excluded: No claim about client requests accepted during the window and no safety claim about committed entries.
Transfers to members absent from the configuration entirely remain unexercised.

scope.description: One follower of a three-voter configuration is driven through real AppendEntries RPCs on its transport while a single heartbeat is executed on a separate goroutine, as the fast-path contract permits. A stable store holds the heartbeat's term write until the main thread has persisted the newer term; the run records the persisted term sequence, the node's current term before and after, and the log and FSM contents at the affected indexes after a stale-leader request.
assumptions: The heartbeat is delivered by invoking the registered processHeartbeat handler on a separate goroutine, which is what NetworkTransport's connection handler does; the in-memory transport ignores the registration, so the transport's own dispatch is not exercised.
The stable store delays, but never corrupts or fails, one currentTerm write, modelling a slow store write that completes after a newer term has been persisted.

The term 2 and term 4 AppendEntries requests are supplied by the harness to represent a leader that has committed those indexes elsewhere; their commit indexes are asserted by the request, not produced by a quorum of real nodes.
Election and lease timeouts are raised to 30 s so the follower does not campaign during the sequence.
excluded: No attempt to measure how often the interleaving occurs in a real deployment; the probe only establishes that the interleaving is reachable when a store write is delayed.
No real partition or multi-node cluster is used, and the stale leader's authority is modelled by crafted requests.

basis.prefix: The harness builds an in-memory stable/log store whose SetUint64 blocks one chosen currentTerm value, bootstraps a three-voter configuration containing the local node, and starts NewRaft with 30 s election and lease timeouts so the node stays a follower. It first commits entries 2 and 3 at term 2 through trans.AppendEntries on the real consumer path, then installs the blocking hook for term 3 and starts r.processHeartbeat on a goroutine with a heartbeat carrying term 3. Once the hook reports that the term 3 write is in flight, the harness sends a term 4 AppendEntries with entry 4 and leader commit 4 through the transport, waits for it to apply, then releases the term 3 write. It records the current term before and after the release, the persisted term and the sequence of term writes, and finally sends the stale term 3 leader's AppendEntries carrying conflicting entries 4 and 5 with leader commit 5, recording whether that request was accepted, the log payloads at indexes 4 and 5, the FSM payloads at those indexes, the applied and commit indexes, and whether the applied payload at index 4 differs from the log payload there.
basis.responsibility: Raft requires a server's persisted current term never to decrease and its applied log prefix never to be replaced. The library owns both: it persists the term, it decides when to raise it, and it performs the truncation that can remove an entry. A transport contract that permits concurrent heartbeat delivery does not relax those duties, so the library must make the term update safe against the concurrency it authorises.

comparisons.description: The persisted current term must not fall below a term the node already adopted; a true value contradicts it.
After the regression, the stale leader's conflicting entries must not replace an entry already applied at a higher term; a true value contradicts it.

scope.description: Two hundred attempts per case on a single follower of a three-voter configuration. Each attempt reads the node's current term, starts a fast-path heartbeat carrying that term plus one on its own goroutine, concurrently sends an AppendEntries carrying the term plus two (with one entry and a matching previous-log index) through the real consumer path, waits for both, and counts the attempt as an inversion when the node's term afterwards is below the higher request's term. The first case leaves the stable store undelayed; the second adds a uniform 0-2 ms delay to every current-term write.
assumptions: One node runs; the two peers are addresses only, so each attempt's higher-term request is a supplied leader message rather than a real election outcome.
The heartbeat is delivered by invoking the registered handler on its own goroutine, matching the classification and direct invocation that NetworkTransport performs for this request shape.
The undelayed case is not a control for absence of the defect; it measures how often the race occurs when the store adds no latency of its own.
Attempts run sequentially on the same node and reuse its log; terms advance across attempts and are re-read each time.
excluded: No consequence measurement here: this execution only counts term inversions; the truncation consequence was measured separately in the forced-ordering execution.
No multi-node cluster, no real transport framing and no concurrent client load.

basis.prefix: The harness builds an in-memory stable/log store whose SetUint64 optionally sleeps a uniformly random interval up to a configured maximum before persisting the current term, bootstraps a three-voter configuration containing the local node, and starts NewRaft with 30 s election and lease timeouts so the node stays a follower. For each attempt it reads r.CurrentTerm() and r.LastIndex(), starts r.processHeartbeat on a goroutine with a heartbeat carrying current+1, sends an AppendEntries carrying current+2, the last log index as PrevLogEntry with its stored term, one entry at the next index and leader commit at that index, then waits for both to finish and records whether the current term is below current+2. Each case emits a case event with the attempt count and maximum delay and a result event with the inversion count.
basis.responsibility: Raft requires a server's persisted current term never to decrease. The library owns the term update and it authorises concurrent heartbeat execution through the transport contract, so the update must remain correct under the concurrency it permits regardless of how the store is timed.

comparisons.description: With no added store delay, no attempt may end below the term the main thread persisted.
With 0-2 ms write jitter, no attempt may end below the term the main thread persisted.

semantic_changes: target_role_in_own_config now answers what the target believed when the transfer was requested, which the earlier receipts could not establish.

scope.description: The same two leadership-transfer cases on real four-voter in-memory clusters: the trigger demotes a non-leader member before LeadershipTransferToServer names it, the control leaves it a voter. After the demotion the harness polls the demoted member's own GetConfiguration until its role changes, records how long that took, and only then requests the transfer, so the case event's role value and the per-sample candidate/leaderless counts describe the state at transfer time.
assumptions: All members run the captured code on the in-memory transport with inmemConfig timeouts (Heartbeat/Election/Lease 50 ms).

The demotion poll waits up to 3 s for the target's own configuration view to report the new role; a case that never converges is recorded with demotion_converged=false and the transfer proceeds anyway.
A leaderless sample means no member reported Leader at that instant, sampled about every 10 ms over roughly 4.7 s.
Both cases run in one execution; each builds and closes its own cluster.
excluded: No claim about client requests during the window and no safety claim about committed entries.
Transfers to members absent from the configuration entirely remain unexercised.

Both now also read the target's own configuration view before the transfer and sample every member's State() every 10 ms for the watch window, recording candidate samples, leaderless samples and terms.
assumptions: All members run the captured code on the in-memory transport with inmemConfig timeouts (Heartbeat/Election/Lease 50 ms).
The demotion call is completed and 200 ms elapse before the transfer; the harness records what the target itself believes rather than asserting convergence.
A leaderless sample means no member reported Leader at that instant; samples are 10 ms apart, so a shorter gap can still be missed.
Both cases run in one execution; each builds and closes its own cluster.
excluded: No claim about client requests accepted during the window and no safety claim about committed entries.
Transfers to members absent from the configuration entirely remain unexercised.

parameters.trigger_target: member demoted to non-voter before the transfer

after.description: The same two leadership-transfer cases on real four-voter in-memory clusters: the trigger demotes a non-leader member before LeadershipTransferToServer names it, the control leaves it a voter. After the demotion the harness polls the demoted member's own GetConfiguration until its role changes, records how long that took, and only then requests the transfer, so the case event's role value and the per-sample candidate/leaderless counts describe the state at transfer time.
assumptions: All members run the captured code on the in-memory transport with inmemConfig timeouts (Heartbeat/Election/Lease 50 ms).

The demotion poll waits up to 3 s for the target's own configuration view to report the new role; a case that never converges is recorded with demotion_converged=false and the transfer proceeds anyway.
A leaderless sample means no member reported Leader at that instant, sampled about every 10 ms over roughly 4.7 s.
Both cases run in one execution; each builds and closes its own cluster.
excluded: No claim about client requests during the window and no safety claim about committed entries.

parameters.trigger_target: member demoted to non-voter before the transfer, after its own view converges

prefix.before: Each case calls MakeClusterCustom with four bootstrapped voters, waits for c.Leader(), selects the first non-leader raft as target, and reads target.GetConfiguration() to record whether the target itself sees its suffrage as voter, nonvoter, absent or unknown. The trigger then calls leader.DemoteVoter(targetID, 0, 5s) and sleeps 200 ms; the control skips demotion. Both call leader.LeadershipTransferToServer(targetID, target.localAddr) and record the future's error and duration, then sample target.State() and every member's State() every 10 ms for five seconds, emitting future_ok, future_error, future_ms, target_ever_leader, final_leader_is_target, candidate_samples, leaderless_samples, no_leader_ms_sampled, samples, target_term_after and other_member_term_max_after.
prefix.after: Each case calls MakeClusterCustom with four bootstrapped voters, waits for c.Leader(), selects the first non-leader raft as target, and records roleBefore from the target's own GetConfiguration. The trigger then calls leader.DemoteVoter(targetID, 0, 5s) and polls the target's own configuration every 10 ms for up to 3 s until it reports nonvoter, recording demotion_converged and demotion_converge_ms; the control skips demotion. Both then read the target's role again as target_role_in_own_config, emit the case event, call leader.LeadershipTransferToServer(targetID, target.localAddr), record the future outcome, and sample target.State() and every member's State() every 10 ms for five seconds.

responsibility.before: The library owns target eligibility: it holds the latest configuration, its automatic path already excludes non-voters, and its documentation states that a follower which cannot be promoted will fail gracefully. A caller naming a configured member therefore relies on the library either to refuse an ineligible target or to report an outcome that matches what happened to authority.
responsibility.after: The library owns target eligibility: it holds the latest configuration, its automatic path already excludes non-voters, and its documentation states that a follower which cannot be promoted will fail gracefully. A caller naming a configured member relies on the library either to refuse an ineligible target or to report an outcome matching what happened to authority.

before.description: Control: a transfer to a voter must install that voter as leader.
Control: a transfer that installs the named voter must complete without error.
A transfer to a member the configuration marks as a non-voter cannot be promoted, so the documented graceful failure requires an error; a successful future contradicts it.
If the transfer is admitted as successful, the named target must hold leadership; a target that never leads contradicts the transfer's stated purpose.

after.description: Control: a transfer to a voter must install that voter as leader.
Control: a transfer that installs the named voter must complete without error.
A transfer to a member whose own configuration view now says non-voter cannot be promoted, so the documented graceful failure requires an error.
If the transfer is admitted as successful, the named target must hold leadership.

experiments.revision_reason: The target's suffrage view is now read after DemoteVoter returns and polled every 10 ms until it reports the new role, instead of being read before the demotion. Case events add target_role_before, demotion_converged and demotion_converge_ms; case names, admissions and assertions are unchanged.
